inspiration: Sudden death as a palette swap: theme.cfg has separate sd-* keys for water and music, and sudden-death art variants exist (Themes/Hell/theme.cfg lines 4-10; SDWater.svg, SDClouds.svg, SDDroplet.png). When the timer runs out the zone reskins. Keep the phase swap; use our own hue and sound cue.
Theme as a data folder: one folder with a config (sky, border, water top and bottom, opacity, music, cloud count, placed objects). Keep the data-driven zone skin; use our own palette and object list.
Tall splash sheet: Themes/Hell/Splash.png (160 x 500) gives impact frames in one strip. Keep the tall narrow strip; change shape and colour.
Head overlays on a fixed 64-pixel grid: Graphics/Hats/AkuAku.png (64 x 512) stacks head-gear frames in one strip. Keep one overlay per head slot; change silhouettes and ornament.
Tall grave strips: Graphics/Graves/Badger.png (32 x 256). A fallen unit keeps a marker in the world. Keep the narrow tall marker; change the design.

Scripted modes over a normal map: Scripts/Multiplayer/Racer.hwp, Construction_Mode.hwp, Continental_supplies.hwp. A mode is a script that changes objectives on the same map. Keep the idea; write our own objectives and rewards.
Themed name pools per costume: Names/README.md describes a hat config that selects a name list. Keep per-costume name pools; write our own lists.

briefs.label: sudden-death palette swap
briefs.why: the zone turns hostile when time runs out, so the endgame reads at a glance
briefs.keep: phase swap of water and music; separate sudden-death art variants
briefs.change: our own hue, water shape and sound cue; never the same colours

briefs.label: fallen-unit marker strip
briefs.why: a narrow tall marker stays in the world after a unit falls and reads from a distance
briefs.keep: tall narrow strip; one marker per fallen unit
briefs.change: our own marker design, not an animal tombstone; our own crack and glow

briefs.label: head overlay strip
briefs.why: a costume overlay swaps head gear without new body art
briefs.keep: fixed-width overlay grid; one overlay per head slot
briefs.change: our own head silhouettes and ornament; different proportions

briefs.change: our own objectives, rewards and names
